title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signals interest in returning if company board chooses
text:
NEW YORK (AP) — Nvidia on Tuesday rejected Jensen Huang’s offer to return as CEO, putting to rest for now any possible reinstatement of the celebrated artificial intelligence billionaire and industry evangelist, despite pressure from Silicon Valley and President Donald Trump’s support.
The embattled company’s board of directors “unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call before yielding to Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who is running the company as a permanent replacement is sought.
The rejection caps a whirlwind few days triggered by Huang’s admission to extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman and suspected spy for the country, his stunning ouster and a surprising split in the Trump administration over the fate of the disgraced business leader.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a wholesale cleaning at Nvidia on Sunday, only for Trump to come out in support of Huang’s return the next day despite investigations into whether Nvidia had allowed AI chips banned from China to slip through the cracks because of the alleged spy at the center of the controversy.
Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said in a social media post that if the board decided that his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and the country, he would be “honored to answer these calls.” He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life.
Company reports blowout financial results
The turmoil notwithstanding, Nvidia blew past Wall Street expectations for the third quarter, pulling in $116 billion in revenue, double the level from a year ago. The company also posted net income of $2.70 per share, beating estimates of $2.48 per share.
Nvidia stock shot up 5.2% in after-hours trading.
Referring to Huang’s replacement, Jones said, “We want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.”
Some tech industry figures, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, called for the reinstatement of Huang, a high-profile booster for the AI industry who oversaw Nvidia’s development as the key provider of chips driving advanced AI models.
Huang said he received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return.
A “Stand with Jensen” petition set up last week gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other Silicon Valley supporters.
In comments Monday, Trump suggested that the ex-CEO could return, saying Huang “learned a big lesson” and that he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.
The Chinese businesswoman whom Huang was seeing and who reportedly had links to Chinese intelligence was an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, a company being investigated by the U.S. for allegedly violating U.S. export controls by illegally diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies.
Huang faces questioning by Congress
Also Tuesday, key House lawmakers said that Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the company faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.
Huang will appear before congressional committees on Dec. 1, followed by the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, on Dec. 2.
“The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips,” said a statement from the chairmen of three House committees with oversight of China and intelligence issues, referring to the People’s Republic of China.
Huang also is expected to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, two people familiar with the matter said.
In the statement detailing its August-to-October results, Nvidia said revenue in a key business segment — data centers — more than doubled to $107.6 billion. It also projected that revenue for the current quarter running through January would hit $130 billion, more than Wall Street had expected.
Nvidia’s advanced chips are in high demand because they’re essential for cloud computing and data centers that underpin the AI boom, but they face restrictions on their sale to China.
Meanwhile, Nvidia said it’s creating a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance following the revelations about Huang. Trump said it was “good” that Nvidia had created the new committee.
“Yes, that’s a good idea. It’s a great company,” Trump said shortly after arriving Tuesday evening in the Philippine capital of Manila, where he participated in a photo opportunity with the leaders of Australia, India and Japan. “It’s a great idea.”
Nvidia later that day signaled it was already moving ahead without Huang.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating,” interim CEO Kress said at the end of the quarterly conference call with investors. “We’ve got this.”
___
Chan reported from London. Associated Press writers Darlene Superville, Seung Min Kim and Kevin Freking in Washington, Alex Veiga in Los Angeles and Josh Boak in Shenzhen, China, contributed.

title: South Portland extends city office closure through Thursday
text:
South Portland city offices and the library will remain closed through Thursday because of a cyberattack that has affected city services since Monday.
The city said on Monday that it first discovered a cybersecurity issue late Saturday night, and a preliminary assessment “indicates cybercriminal activity” and that “the majority of city data is unaffected by this cyberattack.”
The city said in an update Tuesday that City Hall, the assessing office and the library will remain closed through Thursday. That means the former two, which are closed on Fridays due to the city’s four-day workweek, won’t reopen until Monday at the earliest.
The city’s computer and phone systems, as well as some online administrative portals and mapping services, will be unavailable until the outage is resolved. City officials don’t know how long the network will be down.
South Portland officials say they have been coordinating with multiple state and federal agencies, as well as an independent forensic examiner.
“It’s all hands on deck,” Mike Dery, the city’s IT director, said in a Monday statement.
In-person credit card payments and receipts at some city facilities also may be affected by the outage. South Portland’s online billing system, Citizen Self Service, has been experiencing unrelated outages since late last week, the city said.
The city noted Monday that police, fire and EMS services have not been impacted.
Some services, such as vehicle registration renewal, can be completed online.
Because of the issues, the property tax due date has been postponed until Nov. 23.

title: Another busy Thanksgiving travel week expected despite high airfare, gas costs
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
FORT COLLINS, Colo. (AP) - Pricey plane tickets and expensive gasoline are expected to keep some Americans from traveling this Thanksgiving, but not enough to make much difference in airport security lines and highway traffic, AAA said Monday.
The auto club federation predicted that 81.5 million people would travel at least 50 miles (80 kilometers) from home between the Tuesday before Thanksgiving and the Monday after the holiday.
That’s about 121,000 fewer than traveled domestically over Thanksgiving last year, or a one-tenth of a percent decline, AAA said in its annual forecast. If proven accurate, the small drop would end three years of record-setting Thanksgiving travel that followed the COVID-19 pandemic, according to AAA’s calculations.
“After three years of record highs, the number of travelers is slightly lower partly because of higher travel costs this year. But travelers won’t notice much of a difference,” AAA Travel Vice President Stacey Barber said in a statement.
Officials: Normal air traffic expected after ground stop
AAA prepared its forecast weeks before problems with U.S. air traffic control communications and radar feeds on Friday prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to impose a nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours and disrupted weekend flights.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford said they expected air traffic to normalize well before the start of the Thanksgiving travel rush.
AAA doesn’t think Friday’s unusually long ground stop will have a major impact on Thanksgiving travel unless it happens again, spokesperson Aixa Diaz said.
“Travelers are resilient, and from what AAA has seen in the past, it takes a lot to keep holiday travelers home,” Diaz wrote in an email Sunday.
As in past years, AAA expects the vast majority of holiday travelers to opt for car trips over flights. Meanwhile, it expects buses, trains and cruise ships will serve 4% more passengers than last year combined.
Flights got more expensive as airlines’ jet fuel costs increased
Last November, a government shutdown that led the FAA to order flight cuts at 40 of the busiest U.S. airports created extra stress for airline passengers with Thanksgiving week tickets.
Air travelers who didn’t cancel their plans were rewarded; Congress ended the longest shutdown in history, and the FAA lifted its order 10 days before Thanksgiving.
This year, fuel prices that surged during the U.S. war with Iran are a concern. The overall inflation that influenced this month’s midterm elections may also have made some Americans more cautious about venturing far afield for their Thanksgiving meals.
With U.S. airlines spending more on jet fuel, airfares were more than 22% higher in September than the same month a year earlier, according to the most recent government data. Carriers also raised fees for checked bags.
Visa’s economic research group said an analysis of September credit card transactions revealed that spending on plane tickets and related travel for trips starting between Nov. 1 and Jan. 15 were down from a year earlier for households of every income level except those earning more than $200,000.
Aviation analytics firm Cirium said Thanksgiving flight bookings were running 1.6% behind last year as of late October.
Gasoline could set a Thanksgiving Day price record
Compared to last year, round-trip domestic flights booked through AAA for the Thanksgiving period were 17% more expensive, averaging $800 per ticket.
AAA expects nearly 6 million people to fly from Nov. 24 through Nov. 30, about 12,000 fewer than last year. Three Florida cities — Orlando, Fort Lauderdale and Miami — are the top three domestic destinations for Thanksgiving flights, the auto club said.
Other organizations have come up with different projections based on the data they reviewed. Trade organization Airlines for America said it expected U.S. carriers to serve more passengers during the same seven-day period, though it did not specify if that includes international flights.
The group said airfares have risen much more modestly than jet fuel prices this year.
Gasoline prices have fallen over the past week, but motorists can expect to pay more than last year heading to and from Thanksgiving destinations, AAA’s forecast said. Regular gas averaged $3.82 a gallon on Sunday compared to $3.08 a year earlier, AAA said.
If prices hold, gasoline would be more expensive this Thanksgiving Day than any previous. AAA’s previous Thanksgiving Day record was $3.58 in 2022.
___
AP writers Lisa Leff in London and Rebecca Boone in Boise, Idaho, contributed to this story.

title: Here's where tax hikes will hit hardest across Penobscot County
text:
Clifton taxpayers will owe Penobscot County nearly 60% more next year, the steepest jump in a county where most towns are taking a bigger hit than the county’s own 23% tax hike.
The figures are the first town-by-town look at what years of bad budgeting at the county are now costing residents. Penobscot County shortchanged its jail starting in 2021 and drained roughly $11 million from its reserves to cover the gaps. Now, a year after a nearly 20% hike, the bill for fully funding the jail is landing on towns, and local officials say they may have to cut their own budgets to keep tax rates from rising.
The 23.36% jump, driven mostly by healthcare and jail costs, won’t land evenly. Each town’s share is based on its property value, so towns where values climbed fastest will pay the most. Bradford and Lowell are set for jumps of 51% and 45%, while Old Town, where values fell, will see the smallest rise.
When a town’s total property value grows faster than the county average, it pays more the following year, Penobscot County Treasurer Glenn Mower said. Most towns won’t know what that means for residents’ tax bills until their own budgets are done.
In Clifton, Select Board Member John Williams said it will be hard for residents to afford the higher cost. Williams sits on the county’s budget advisory committee and voted against most of the budget earlier this month, saying savings could have been found.
On the other end is Old Town, which pays nearly 4% of all county taxes. Its property values dropped, so its share will go up 7.4%, the smallest rise in the county.
In Veazie, the county tax is slated to rise 26.38%. The county tax is only part of a property tax bill, but residents see their bill as one number, and that leaves local officials to explain the county’s budget spike, Town Manager Mark Leonard said.
“While municipalities have little control over the county assessment, we are ultimately responsible for incorporating that expense into our budgets and explaining the impact to our residents,” he said.
Taxpayers are paying for essential county services that shouldn’t be compromised, Leonard said. But two years of substantial jumps should bring more scrutiny of the county budget. County departments can make a case for more employees, resources or equipment, but commissioners should spend more time reviewing which costs are justifiable, he said.
“At some point, we need to recognize that taxpayers cannot continually be expected to absorb double-digit increases in government spending,” Leonard said. “The question should not simply be what the county government needs, but what the people paying the bills can reasonably afford.”
Most other Greater Bangor towns will see their taxes rise roughly in line with the county budget. Orrington’s county tax is set to rise 21.87% and Hermon’s 28.53%. Together, the two towns will send an additional $612,888 to the county next year.
Neither town knows yet how the tax hikes will affect residents’ bills.
Orrington’s final tax tally includes 423 variables, and the county is just one of them, Town Manager Chris Backman said. The town knows how much more it will owe the county, but every other cost is also going up. Backman and the select board will go through every expense, including the county tax, during budget talks, he said.
In Hermon, it’s too early to say how much each taxpayer will pay the county, Town Manager Stephen Fields said. Town and school budgets are in the early stages, so it’s still unknown how the local tax rate will change.
Penobscot County Commissioners David Marshall, Dan Tremble and Andre Cushing will vote on the 2027 budget Wednesday, after a public hearing at 10 a.m.

title: Harlem Globetrotters to perform in Augusta, Bangor and Portland on Rivalry Tour
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - The award-winning Harlem Globetrotters will perform in three Maine cities in February as part of the Harlem Globetrotters: Rivalry Tour, which begins next month.
The Maine shows are scheduled for:
- Feb. 9 at the Augusta Civic Center in Augusta
- Feb. 10 at the Cross Insurance Center in Bangor
- Feb. 11 at the Cross Insurance Arena in Portland
The tour begins Friday, Dec. 18, and extends across more than 200 domestic markets and more than 150 international markets.
The game adds two new rival teams joining the Washington Generals, bringing new competition and new challenges. Fans can vote live on all-new game challenges and help shape moments of competition on the court.
The Globetrotters are Guinness World Record holders and members of the Naismith Hall of Fame.
Tickets can be purchased at harlemglobetrotters.com.

title: Man killed in Maine plane crash
text:
A man was killed in a Monday afternoon plane crash in Sweden.
The single-engine Cessna 182 took off from Fyreburg Airport about 3:45 p.m., according to ABC affiliate WMTW.
The plane then crashed near Smarts Hill Road in the Oxford County town of Sweden, the TV station reported.
The pilot, who was the only person aboard, died in the crash, according to WMTW.
The crash remains under investigation.

title: Obituary: Jedda Lorraine Martel
text:
OLD ORCHARD BEACH – Jedda Lorraine Martel, 81, of MacIntosh Lane, Old Orchard Beach, passed away peacefully at her home surrounded by her family. Born in Biddeford on Jan. 14, 1945, the daughter of Gerald and Rita Bouchard Littlefield.
Jedda attended Thornton Academy and met her husband, Richard Martel, while working as a candy striper at Webber Hospital; they married in 1965 and operated Sansoucy-Blais Funeral Home in Biddeford until they moved back to Jedda’s childhood home in Camp Ellis in 1979.
Together, they raised their children while Jedda ran Langevine’s Market, and Richard engaged in commercial fishing. Langevine’s was a beloved local hub where fishermen gathered, shared news, and enjoyed community life. Jedda later worked at Lou’s Market which became known as Saco Bay Variety, working early mornings and greeting everyone with her contagious smile and genuine interest in the lives of all whom she crossed paths with.
Jedda was a beloved Camp Ellis resident, former market owner, and community leader whose 2026 role as HarborFest Grand Marshal honored her decades of service and the enduring traditions of Saco’s working waterfront. Jedda’s decades of involvement in her community made her a respected figure in Camp Ellis, embodying the area’s values of cooperation, tradition, and support for those who work on the water. Jedda loved Camp Ellis and was a true historian of life at the beach, on the working waterfront and summer and local residents.
Jedda is survived by her husband Richard of 61 years; her daughter Doreen Alling and her husband Ken of Camp Ellis, her son Dale and his wife Linda of Old Orchard Beach; her grandchildren Madeline Chamberlin and her husband Matthew Bennett-Hall of Montreal, Summer Chamberlin of Boulder, Colo. and Shauna Martel and their fiancé Sage Thayer of Biddeford; her sisters Carolyn Pierson of Florida and Judy Couture and her husband Leo of Georgia.
Calling hours will be held from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, at Dennett, Craig & Pate Funeral Home, 365 Main Street, Saco, followed by an 11 a.m. memorial service officiated by Rev. Dave Dalzell and burial at Laurel Hill Cemetery.
Memorial donations may be made in Jedda’s honor to:
National Kidney
Foundation
Finance Dept.
30 East 33rd St.
New York, NY 10016

title: Feds sue to block Portland-based veterinary company’s $3.5B merger
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
The Federal Trade Commission has sued to block Portland-based Covetrus Inc., a global veterinary supply and services company, from acquiring its closest competitor in a $3.5 billion merger that’s been in the works for more than nine months.
The FTC says the deal to buy MWI Veterinary Supply Inc. of Boise, Idaho, would merge the two largest distributors of veterinary supplies in the U.S., according to a complaint filed Friday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
The combined firm would drive up costs for veterinary clinics, decrease service quality and increase prices for pet owners, said Daniel Guarnera, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Competition.
“These two companies are engaged in fierce head-to-head competition, and Covetrus wants to eliminate its closest competitor rather than compete for veterinary clinic customers,” Guarnera said in a statement.
Covetrus and MWI distribute products used in veterinary clinics, including pharmaceuticals, surgical supplies and thousands of other products and services, the FTC stated. Their customers range from independent, single-veterinarian practices to large corporate accounts with hundreds of clinics across the country.
Both companies have national distribution networks that allow them to deliver products quickly and offer discounts and rebates that smaller rivals cannot match, according to the complaint.
The complaint is joined by the attorneys general of Maine, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon and Texas.
In its own statement Friday, Covetrus said it will defend the merger in court.
“Together, Covetrus and MWI will make it easier and more efficient for practices to access the products, technology and support they need, while investing in innovation, maintaining service and supply chain reliability, and lowering the cost of serving veterinary practices,” Covetrus said.
Covetrus and its owners, CD&R and TPG, a U.S. and European private equity platform that acquired the Maine company in 2022, announced the merger plan in February.
The agreement valued MWI at $3.5 billion and would give its parent company, Cencora Inc. of Conshohocken, Pennsylvania, $1.25 billion in cash, $800 million in preferred equity and a 34.3% noncontrolling stake in the combined company.
“Cencora disagrees with the FTC’s decision to sue and is prepared to defend the case alongside Covetrus to complete the pending merger,” a spokesperson for Cencora said in an email Tuesday. “We remain confident in the merits of the transaction and the benefits it will bring to the animal health market.”

title: The Unspoken Connection Between Domestic Abuse and Suicide
text:
Domestic abuse and suicide touch many lives but often don’t get talked about in the same conversations. People feel deeply uncomfortable around these topics and avoid discussing them because they invoke societal taboos. They are very intractable problems. They also intersect in real ways, and this connection creates elevated risk of harm and death for individuals, families and the general public.
Survivor suicide
According to the American Psychological Association, dying by suicide is sometimes perceived by victims as their only escape from egregious domestic abuse, which often includes strangulation, sexual and financial abuse, and battering. In addition, many survivors suffer head trauma from assaults, resulting in cognitive and mood disorders that can lead to suicidal ideation because of physiological changes. A 2024 study linked brain injury plus non-fatal strangulation (both commonly experienced by abuse victims) with self-harm and suicide, saying, “Those who experience both acquired brain injury and non-fatal strangulation injuries have been found to be more likely to self-harm, with 57% of respondents in recent research stating that they had thought about ending their lives and 47% reporting a prior attempt to do so.”
Murder-Suicide
Another dimension of risk lies in the abuser’s mental state. Research on domestic violence has shown that when abusive people talk about or threaten suicide, it directly increases the chance of a murder-suicide. Over the last decade, there have been over 6,000 murder-suicides by gun in the United States. Most abusers who consider suicide plan to kill their partner first, usually with a gun, and this often happens around the time the partner tries to leave. An abuser’s access to a gun greatly increases the risk of intimate partner homicide, and an abuser’s threat of suicide is recognized as a high‑risk indicator in tools like the Danger Assessment, an instrument used by trained professionals to assess a person’s risk of being killed by their partner. The link between murder and suicide is double-pronged: Experiencing domestic abuse can lead victims to be suicidally despondent, and when an abuser is suicidal, this puts their partner at a higher risk of dying in a murder-suicide.
Elder abuse and murder-suicide
Murder-suicides occurring in older adult couples are especially troubling and culturally nuanced. They are often framed by families or well-meaning others as “mutual pacts,” “mercy killings,” and otherwise consensual arrangements between the victim and perpetrator. In reality, evidence has shown that the victim was often experiencing abuse, perhaps for many years, was unaware of the plan, and did not consent or was unable to consent (e.g., due to advanced dementia or cognitive decline).
Maine’s Domestic Abuse Homicide Review Panel has repeatedly stressed how damaging this misleading rhetoric is. Describing a killing as an act of "mercy" or "love" obscures underlying dynamics of intimate partner violence (IPV), control or desperation. According to a study at the University of Utah, many older-adult murder-suicides involve a long history of abuse, isolation or a partner's unwillingness to seek help or lose control over their spouse's care. This is often deliberately played down by those close to the family because of shame and grief. Obituaries use euphemistic language, saying the victim “passed away unexpectedly at her home,” or “they died tragically at home.” This understandable attempt to soften and mitigate stigma and trauma exists alongside public recognition of the circumstances, such as news coverage, vigils and other expressions of outrage and grief, which creates a strange dissonance.
DV, mass shootings, and suicide
Finally, there is a strong link between mass shootings and domestic violence. Researchers in criminology, public health and psychology have shown that domestic abuse, suicide and mass shootings are part of the same social illness, and not isolated phenomena. Scholars and law enforcement analysts increasingly view domestic violence as a precursor to mass casualty events, so while not every abuser experiencing suicidal ideation is necessarily working up to murder or mass shooting, the reverse association has been confirmed again and again. A 2020 Bloomberg analysis found fifty to sixty percent of mass shooters have a documented history of domestic violence, or have killed their partner or other family member in the attack.
Recognizing this triangular relationship has shifted public safety strategies toward early intervention, including Extreme Risk Protection Orders (Red Flag Laws), that allow courts, at a family’s request, to temporarily remove firearms from individuals displaying suicidal behavior or domestic abuse threats. It is beneficial to restrict access to firearms for individuals subject to domestic violence restraining orders (in Maine called Protection from Abuse orders), and to educate law enforcement and workplace/school threat assessment teams to view domestic abuse and self-harm threats not as isolated private matters, but as warning signs of potential targeted violence. As a society, we must recognize the very real danger to people and communities from domestic abuse and murder-suicide.
While the main activity of domestic violence advocacy is supporting individual survivors, we recognize the intricate connections among these different forms of violence. As part of the movement to end domestic violence and other forms of oppression, we will continue to work closely with professionals in other fields, like law enforcement, the judicial system, mental healthcare and state lawmakers to foster prevention, accountability and education so that people and communities can be safer.
New Hope Midcoast is one of Maine’s Regional Domestic Violence Resource Centers and a member of the Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence. Our nonprofit organization supports people impacted by domestic abuse, dating violence, and stalking through housing and legal advocacy, education and prevention programs, and a 24/7 helpline. New Hope serves Sagadahoc, Lincoln, Knox and Waldo counties and empowers clients by providing options and treating everyone with care and respect.

title: She married at 16. Now she’s fighting to end child marriage in Ohio
text:
CLEVELAND, Oh. (InvestigateTV) - Protecting children from forced marriages in recent years, several states have taken action to stop what some call abuse.
Ohio’s current marriage law
Before 2019, Ohio had no minimum age to marry. The current minimum is 17. Ohio Senate Bill 341 would raise that age to 18 years old.
According to the nonprofit Unchained at Last, which advocates for banning child marriage, more than 5,000 children in Ohio have been married as minors since 2000.
Seventeen states have already banned child marriage, the organization reports. Nationwide, nearly 315,000 minors were legally married between 2000 and 2021.
Currently in Ohio, 17-year-olds cannot marry anyone older than 21.
Survivor speaks out
Stephanie Lowry survived child marriage and now advocates for others. She grew up in a religious family in Ohio. After her father died unexpectedly, her mother struggled, and her older sister married a man she had just met at age 19. Stephanie went to live with her sister and later became pregnant.
“I was 15 at the time I became pregnant. So, it would have been statutory rape for him,” Lowry said. “So one of the options is you need to marry her. And then that statutory rape goes away because you married her.”
A month after her 16th birthday, Lowry said her mother found a legal pathway that allowed the marriage.
“And at that time my mom looked up some laws around the marriage and back then you could be 16 with your parental signature and a psychologist letter,” Lowry said.
In 2001, four months pregnant, Lowry married the baby’s father at a courthouse. He was 19 years old.
“So, you’re going through having a baby, having a wedding with zero joy around it, just shame built up around you,” she said.
‘Your brain isn’t developed’
Once married, Lowry’s husband, not her mother, became her legal guardian.
“Basically, you’re just surviving in it. Because your brain isn’t developed to understand all the adults that were supposed to protect you can sometimes fail you,” Lowry said.
Lowry says the relationship turned abusive. At 17, with a 6-month-old baby, she called police after a fight became physical. She said they did not know what to do.
“He took me to the police station, and it was me and my son sitting there and he bought me a bag of Skittles. And just like a child, because I was a child,” she said.
Lowry could not return to her mother’s home or enter a battered women’s shelter because she was not 18. Foster care would have separated her from her baby. The shelter gave her and her baby a temporary placement, but their time there ran out. Because she was a minor, she could not independently file for divorce.
“Ultimately, I had to end up back with my abuser husband until I turned 18. A month after my 18th birthday, I was able to file another protection order on top of the other ones I already had on him. And I was able to leave the marriage,” Lowry said.
Life after child marriage
Lowry hid from her ex-husband for years after the divorce. She says he later died by suicide. She eventually rebuilt her life.
“I’ve been married for eight years, and we have a blended family,” she said.
Her son, born when she was 16, is now 24 years old.
“And all the healing I’ve done is where it’s brought me today, where I can be a voice and I can share my story with being vulnerable without any shame that I carried for so many years of being that young mom and a single mom,” Lowry said.
Lowry said Ohio’s current minimum age of 17 would not have protected her in 2001.
“So, the new law would have not protected me in 2001. They need to make it 18, no exceptions, because the new law still did not close the legal loopholes,” she said.
Advocates say child marriage can be a loophole for statutory rape, abuse and child trafficking.

title: Attorneys can no longer bypass security in Maine's courts
text:
Attorneys can no longer bypass security in Maine’s courthouses starting next year.
That move, announced Tuesday morning, aligns with federal courts and other state courts across New England, according to the Maine Judicial Branch.
“The Judicial Branch continuously reviews our security protocols to ensure appropriate measures are in place. We believe this policy change provides greater protection for all people using the courthouse,” Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill said in a statement.
The state court system stopped issuing new security cards back in May, and attorneys whose cards don’t expire by Jan. 1, 2027, can get a refund for the unexpired portion of their card.
Attorneys will be able to show their bar card to skip to the front of security lines, or courthouses may have a separate line just for attorneys.
The change takes effect Jan. 1.

title: Maine electric bills to increase in January
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Central Maine Power and at least some Versant Power customers will see monthly bill increases in the new year.
The Maine Public Utilities Commission announced Tuesday that it accepted final 2027 standard offer bids for CMP and the Versant Maine Public District, setting new rates for residential and business customers. The commission said it will accept final bids for Versant’s Bangor Hydro District on Wednesday.
The average residential CMP customer, using approximately 550 kilowatt-hours of electricity per month, will see an increase of about $4.99 to their monthly bill next year, according to the commission. Customers of Versant’s Maine Public District, using an average of 500 kWh, can expect a roughly $2.30 increase.
While noting the commission cannot control market prices, Acting Commission Chair Patrick Scully said in a written statement that “our staff has taken every step possible to protect consumers from hefty price spikes during a time of extreme price volatility in the energy market.”
“Standard Offer electricity supply accounts for about half of the total residential customer bill in CMP and Versant territories,” the commission’s news release states.
CMP residential and small businesses will go from a rate of 12.72 cents to 13.63 cents per kWh starting in January, while medium businesses will see a small decrease — from a weighted average of 12.37 cents per kWh in 2026 to 12.03 cents per kWh next year, according to the commission.
Residential and small business customers in the Versant Maine Public District will see an increase from 14.88 cents per kWh this year to 15.34 cents per kWh in 2027.
The weighted average for medium businesses in that district will increase from 14.68 cents per kWh to 16.09 cents per kWh in 2027, while large businesses will see a smaller increase, from 17.16 cents per kWh to 17.30 cents per kWh.
The commission noted that the rates for medium and larger businesses can vary by month.
More information on standard offer rates can be found on the commission’s webpage at maine.gov/mpuc.

title: 2-year-old’s heart and lungs to save other young children in need through organ donation
text:
LEXINGTON, Ky. (WKYT/Gray News) - A Kentucky family is preparing for an honor walk for their 2-year-old son ahead of an organ donation at UK Hospital.
Abel Beckler was declared brain dead last Saturday after his parents said he had a seizure and went into cardiac arrest.
“I wish I could hold and hug my little boy just one more time,” Haley Hurt, Abel’s mother, said.
Abel would have turned 3 at the end of the month. His parents said they want to turn their tragedy into miracles for other families through organ donation.
The hospital has matched Abel’s heart and lungs to other young children. Hurt said his liver possibly will go to a 9-month-old baby.
“His liver is possibly going to go to a 9-month-old baby that could get out and see the whole entire world that my little boy didn’t get to finish seeing,” Hurt said.
Abel’s father, Logan Beckler, said Abel had a heart of gold and loved babies. He said the donations give him a small sense of peace.
“The Lord’s work meant for us to be here to make that boy bigger than just how tall he was, and that does fill my heart up some, although it may not fill it all. I believe that was his mission,” Beckler said.
Abel’s parents said the process is opening their eyes to the need for child organ donation. They want parents to know it is an option if they ever deal with the death of a child.
“Through this, we have learned that it is not common, especially here at UK, for a kid to donate organs,” Amber Duerson, Abel’s stepmother, said.
The family said that because of organ donation, this is only the beginning of Abel’s story.
“To be able to wake up every day and know that something of my son is still living and has many years to live,” Hurt said.
The family said funeral arrangements depend on the organ donation process.
On Friday in Estill County, the family will host an Abel-Strong fundraiser to bring family and friends together to honor him, with donations going to the Ronald McDonald House.

title: NSA internal systems experienced outage following routine maintenance, US official confirms
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — An internal network the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline Tuesday after what the agency described as “routine maintenance.”
The problem disrupted the operations of NSANet, a classified internal network used by employees of the agency, according to a defense official who was not authorized to discuss the matter by name and spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity.
“The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” the NSA said in a statement. “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues. NSA’s infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.”
EN ESPAÑOL | Red de comunicaciones de seguridad de EE.UU., altamente clasificada, sufre caída, reporta CNN
The intelligence agency did not provide any additional details on the cause of the outage or the scope of the disruption.
The outage was first reported by CNN.
The NSA episode is among a series of cyber-related disruptions to critical government and private sector functions in the last week, including a system overload Friday that resulted in a ground stop of air traffic in the United States, a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase on Monday that caused ripple effects in the financial system and an internal systems outage at United Airlines that delayed departing flights.
On Tuesday , Apple acknowledged on its system status page that its Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare services suffered full outages after an internal update.
Top Trump administration national security officials said there was no indication that the events are related or attributable to a cyberattack or hostile activity.
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation-state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also Trump’s national security adviser, told reporters while traveling with the president in Asia.
Rubio acknowledged that it was “unsettling to see these reports day after day of some technical failures” and that while the government is always vigilant, each of the recent events “are distinct, and they’re different in their causation — in some cases, highly technical.”
Jay Clayton, the Trump administration’s director of national intelligence, attributed the problem to government institutions and private companies pushing through upgrades of their computer systems around the same time, resulting in periodic technological hiccups.
“Many people are patching their systems,” Clayton said in a CNBC interview Tuesday about the spate of disruptions. ”They know that their legacy systems have vulnerabilities. They’re outdated, they don’t work well with new systems. It is time for an upgrade across our digital infrastructure. And as you patch and upgrade your systems — taking them down and bringing them back up — there are things like this that happen.”
Sen. Mark Warner, the Democratic vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, echoed that assessment.
“AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren’t built to handle that pace of change,” Warner said in a statement. “While we still need to get to the bottom of these incidents, the evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”

Sweetser purchases former Androscoggin Bank building in Lewiston
More mental health services are coming to Lewiston after Sweetser bought the former Androscoggin Bank building in the city late last month.
Sweetser CEO Jayne Van Bramer said the building, located on Lisbon Street, will serve as an on-site pharmacy and provide primary care services, pairing with the nonprofit’s Hope and Healing Center already in the city.
"This is just a terrific addition to our suite, and we're just committed to that community and helping it as much as we can," Van Bramer said.
Van Bramer said the property, estimated at around 35,000ft², cost $750,000.
At the same time, Sweetser is still working to raise money to create Maine’s first psychiatric residential treatment facility.
The project costs roughly $7.9 million. Most of it has already been funded through the state and other fundraising efforts. As of now, Van Bramer says they need about $1 million more to complete funding for the Saco facility.
Van Bramer said they purchased the building in Lewiston amid other fundraising efforts because both projects are desperately needed.
"It's not a question of one or the other," Van Bramer said. We intend to do both, and we will do both."
Sweetser says the plan is to have the Lewiston building up and running in 2027.

title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
text:
Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
Zelenskyy portrayed the operation on the Kerch Bridge as a masterstroke, as Ukrainian forces gradually wore down Russian air defenses for weeks before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.
Zelenskyy didn’t detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said that an arch and a span of the bridge’s road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but its arch was damaged.
Related video: Who's meeting with President Trump for this week's historic nuclear summit in Asia?
The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia’s illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory for Ukrainians.
“The symbol of the occupation has cracked,” the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.
Moscow’s forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital’s main bridges and killing at least two people.
A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022.
U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
Missiles delivered the final blow in the 7-stage operation
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.
Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Flamingo precision-guided missiles delivered the final blow, he said.
Russia’s Investigative Committee said that the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage. It didn't elaborate.
The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that traffic across the bridge was halted but rail traffic was restored by Tuesday afternoon. He didn’t mention any damage.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that “there is no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than it was before.”
Zelenskyy noted that Russia has battered Ukrainian infrastructure, especially the power grid, every day. There were significant power outages in three Ukrainian regions Tuesday, he said.
“We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection,” he said.
Russian air defenses downed 1,441 drones during a second straight night of major Ukrainian attacks, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday.
That was a day after Russia said that it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones in the highest number of interceptions it had reported so far during the war.
Ukraine also attacks industrial areas deep inside Russia
Elsewhere, authorities in Bashkortostan, a Russian region in the southern Ural Mountains, said that defenses repelled a “massive” drone attack on industrial zones in the cities of Ufa and Salavat. All plants there worked as usual, officials said.
However, independent news outlet Astra reported a huge fire at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, nearly 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of the Ukrainian border. The major petrochemical complex has been attacked a number of times before.
In Moscow, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that around 800 drones flew toward the Moscow region overnight. Most were downed far away, and 321 were shot down as they approached the Russian capital.
Russia hits bridges in Ukraine's capital
Seven Russian ballistic missiles hit two of Kyiv's main bridges during the night, Zelenskyy said.
Experts are inspecting the damaged North and South bridges to assess the extent of the destruction, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Both were closed to traffic.
Russian attacks damaged other infrastructure and started fires in four districts of the Ukrainian capital, officials said, as Moscow continues its campaign to make life difficult for Ukrainian civilians.
The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that its forces overnight carried out a major strike using land- and air-based precision weapons and drones on Ukraine’s military industrial facilities, energy, transport and port infrastructure, as well as vessels used for Ukraine's armed forces.
Russian forces launched a combined attack on industrial facilities in three districts of the southern Ukraine region of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and wounding 18 others and leaving a large number of consumers in the region without power, said Mykhailo Semikin, head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration.
The possibility of more talks
Meanwhile, the negotiating teams of Ukraine, the United States, and European partners held a working video call on Monday, during which they discussed the results of recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, and the agenda for the next stage of negotiations, said Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service.
“We aligned our positions and our next joint steps,” Umerov said on Telegram following the conversation.
On the European side, representatives of France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Poland, NATO and the European Commission joined the conversation.
The United States was represented by envoys Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of U.S. forces in Europe, Umerov said.

title: Board of Peace delivers bleak report on Gaza, warning of ceasefire collapse without immediate action
text:
Board of Peace delivers bleak report on Gaza, warning of ceasefire collapse without immediate action
The body overseeing the U.S.-brokered ceasefire in Gaza delivered another bleak report Tuesday on its progress to the United Nations Security Council, warning diplomats of a collapse of the fragile agreement if steps are not taken for full implementation.
The Board of Peace report calls on both Israel and Hamas to uphold the commitments made last year under the agreement and urges the U.N.'s most powerful body to lend its support to the execution.
“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” says the report, a copy of which was obtained by The Associated Press.
It is the latest admonishment from the board in recent weeks as deadly Israeli strikes and the continued blocking of humanitarian aid to Gaza have caused widespread devastation to the civilian population, which the board says is set to face “another winter in tents and rubble.”
“Restrictions imposed by Israel on the entry of supplies and equipment, compounded by funding shortfalls, continued to impede preparedness and response efforts,” the report said, calling for immediate “scaled-up entry of shelter and winterization materials” and approvals for pumps, generators and heavy machinery.
The board's first report was delivered in May by its director-general Nickolay Mladenov, who formerly served as a U.N. Mideast envoy. At the time, Mladenov had acknowledged to the Security Council that the truce brokered by President Donald Trump had stalled since taking effect in October of last year, saying the deadlock over disarming Hamas had paralyzed progress.
The report released this week echoes those same issues six months later, pointing out how continued Israeli strikes in Gaza and Hamas military activity have stalled efforts for both sides to adhere to the road map.
“A ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely,” the report said. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”
Apart from continued fighting, the report laments that the technocratic civil administration the board created to run Gaza on an interim basis has still not been allowed by Israel to take up its job in the territory.
“The absence of decisions by the government of Israel on the necessary conditions and arrangements for the training, deployment and return of civilian police to Gaza continues to impede full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan,” the report said. “The Board of Peace calls on the government of Israel to take these decisions without delay.”
The lack of approvals has, in turn, delayed deployment of an international stabilization force, which is key to Israel’s withdrawal of troops from Gaza, the disarmament of Hamas and the start of reconstruction.
To get things moving, the board appealed to the Security Council to put its full weight behind the agreement it endorsed last year and urge the parties to stop delays.
“Neither party may treat the other’s delay as license for its own inaction, and together these obligations are the only route to Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction at scale,” the report said.
It added that the end result “must lead to the credible pathway to Palestinian self-determination and statehood … and no unilateral step should be allowed to foreclose it.”

title: Shoebox gifts collected in Maine for Operation Christmas Child
text:
BREWER, Maine (WABI) - Churches across Maine are collecting gift-filled shoeboxes for Operation Christmas Child. The gifts are meant for children in need, ages 2 to 14, around the world.
National Collection Week ends Monday.
How the collection works
Lynn Hilyard, area coordinator for Operation Christmas Child, said boxes are arriving from churches, community groups and individuals.
“We are packing shoeboxes for children that go all over the world. We are receiving boxes from churches, community groups, and individuals are bringing them,” Hilyard said.
The shoeboxes hold school supplies, hygiene items, toys, clothing, a jump rope, a ball and a hand-cranked flashlight, according to the script’s on-camera interview. Items should be new, and boxes should be full.
The boxes are counted at the drop-off site and shipped by truck to a processing center. They go to more than 170 countries.
How to donate
Any shoebox or good-quality plastic box can be used. Red and green boxes are available at Calvary Baptist Church in Brewer and at radio station WHCF.
People can also pack a shoebox online year-round at samaritanspurse.org/operation-christmas-child/buildonline. Donors choose items, a boy or girl, and an age group. They can write a note and add a picture. The cost is $30, which includes shipping.
To find a drop-off location, visit samaritanspurse.org .
Church involvement
“Millions of boxes are going to be distributed this year. It’s fun and exciting! Every year there’s a new crop of people that want to get involved and get excited about it,” Phil Mumford, pastor of First Assembly Bangor Church said.
“We believe that the love of God calls us to reach out locally and globally so we have lots of opportunities to reach local but this is an opportunity to reach global and to make an impact in the world. We hope it makes a difference,” Mumford added.

American Airlines flight carrying US senator makes emergency landing
American Airlines Flight 496 from Tampa, Florida, to Washington, D.C., was diverted to Orlando shortly after takeoff, officials said.
The flight that took off Monday afternoon had U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Florida, on board.
Video above: Sen. Ashley Moody recognized Florida man for his heroism in U.S. Senate
A Mayday call was recorded on flight audio following reported engine issues. After declaring an emergency, pilots were able to land safely in Orlando around 3 p.m.
Moody missed Monday's Senate votes because of the incident.
In a statement to Punchbowl News, Moody's office said, "Earlier today the American Airlines flight she was on had engine failure and had to make an emergency landing in Orlando. She got on the next available flight to DC but unfortunely landed just after votes closed. She is grateful to the pilots and crew for getting everyone on board on the ground safely."
The Federal Aviation Administration is now investigating the issue that comes days after a nationwide ground stop halted thousands of flights. The effects are still being felt at airports across the U.S.
United Airlines was forced to delay departing flights after a system outage that lasted nearly two hours Monday afternoon.
Moody, 51, is a native of Plant City, Florida. She served as Florida's attorney general from Jan. 8, 2019, to Jan. 21, 2025.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Moody to the U.S. Senate seat vacated by the resignation of Marco Rubio, who became United States Secretary of State in the Trump administration, in January 2025.
Earlier in November 2026, she won reelection to the U.S. Senate, defeating Democrat Angie Nixon. Moody campaigned alongside President Donald Trump, as her campaign promised voters that she would be a “key supporter” of Trump’s agenda.
On Monday, the Senate took steps to advance a bipartisan permitting reform package closer to final passage by voting to end debate on a managers’ amendment to strengthen provisions of the bill addressing data centers.

title: How to watch out for snakes and other dangerous critters
text:
SCOTTSDALE, Az. (InvestigateTV) — Under decks, inside sheds or even in outdoor equipment, snakes can hide around your yard and in parks.
They’re vital to our ecosystem for hunting insects and rodents, but a bite can mean life or death.
The rattlesnake, which is found in a majority of the U.S. and more common in the southwest, is one species that people should be aware of.
An Arizona grandfather recovered after being bitten by a diamondback rattlesnake during an evening walk near his home.
Gary Takacs, 66, was walking in his neighborhood when he accidentally stepped on a rattlesnake.
“It literally — I just put my left foot down and it responded back with a bite to my ankle. I was wearing running shoes with short socks, no ankle protection, no hiking boots or anything,” Takacs said.
He said the bite felt like a charge of electricity running through his leg.
“Extreme pain, felt the fangs, could feel it and then instantly felt the pain from the bite,” Takacs said.
He was able to walk home a few blocks away, and his wife called 911. Takacs was given a dose of anti-venom and spent the night in a hospital ICU. He is expected to make a full recovery.
“I’m giving my grandkids stories to tell, so maybe they’ll embellish it, make it greater down the road. I just count myself very blessed, very fortunate,” he said.
Takacs, a frequent runner and hiker, wants to share his story and let others know the importance of taking extra precautions this time of year and keeping an eye out for rattlesnakes.
Aries Clark with the Phoenix Herpetological Sanctuary said when the weather heats up, rattlesnakes can pop up anywhere — not just on hiking trails.
“Yesterday I removed a snake from a neighborhood garage, so it is possible for them to enter your home, backyard, all different kinds of areas. It’s really anywhere,” Clark said.
Snake experts recommend that if you see or hear a rattler, step away very slowly.
Takacs said he will be paying more attention from now on.
“I have a head lamp that has LED lamp that lights everything up. If I am going to be up before sunrise or after sunset, I will have lighting, just going to be more aware,” he said.
How to watch out for animals
Giving a snake space applies to all creatures, as many states have more than one type of venomous animal.
Wildlife experts say the best way to tell if a snake is venomous is to learn about the specific species in your area.
“It’s obviously going to be their patterns and their markings and also their habitat,” said Elizabeth Kimble, an Arkansas wildlife expert. “Their head shape and their eye shape is not a 100% definite way to tell if it’s a venomous snake or non-venomous snake and if you’re that close your too close if you don’t know what kind of snake it is.”
Kimble said snakes generally avoid confrontation and usually only strike if provoked.
The reptile is most likely to be found near water in the early morning or late evening.
When you’re in more wooded areas, hiking or working in your garden you should wear closed-toed shoes. Experts suggest keeping yards trimmed low and be cautious around wood or leaf piles.
Experts say to have a professional remove any snakes and in some states it is illegal to kill snakes.

title: Man charged in Palermo killing seeks to bar ‘to-do’ list from evidence
text:
The lawyer for the man charged with the murder of Robert Bruso last year has asked the court to exclude a to-do list and drawings of Bruso’s property that may have been created by the suspect.
Liberty resident Kirby Bradford is charged with murdering Robert Bruso at Bruso’s home in Palermo in February 2025. According to a police affidavit filed in court, Bradford and Bruso had known each other for more than 20 years. Bruso’s friends told police that Bruso often kept large sums of cash in his house, police wrote in the document. Bruso’s body was found by state troopers in April 2025, after friends and family had been unable to contact him for weeks.
Police searched Bradford’s workplace at an equipment rental business in Waterville on July 14, 2025. There, according to the affidavit, they found a diagram of Bruso’s property, with labels such as “garage,” “shed” and “camper.”
They also found a list that said “Stun gun, zip ties, covid masks, take phone, bring him somewhere out of site [sic], duck TAPE for mouth, bag OVER his head.”
In a response to Bradford’s motion to suppress, Assistant Attorney General Mark Rucci wrote that the list is “suggestive of — at the very least — a plan to abduct an individual.”
A forensic handwriting examiner concluded that Bradford wrote the list and the labels in the diagram, Rucci wrote. The examiner said “no conclusion could be reached” regarding whether he drew the diagram. She also said certain markings on the document were not made by Bradford.
The handwriting examiner did not offer an opinion about when the document was created.
Jeremy Pratt, Bradford’s defense attorney, wrote in his motion that the court should prevent the prosecution from showing the document to the jury. Because there is uncertainty about when the document was created, and whether Bradford drew the diagram of Bruso’s house, the document has not been authenticated enough to be admissible, he said.
He also pointed out that the list omits multiple elements of the circumstances of Bruso’s death. When police found Bruso’s body, the holes in his clothing indicated that he had been shot, and wire was wrapped around his belt, according to an affidavit. The list does not mention a plan to shoot or kill anyone, and it does not mention the wire.
If jury members see the document, Pratt said, they may assume that Bradford wrote the words before Bruso’s death and that he drew the diagram, even though it’s not clear whether those are true. They may then assume the document is a plan to kill Bruso.
If the court doesn’t agree to suppress the document, Pratt has an alternative suggestion: the prosecution should not be allowed to tell the jury that Bradford created the diagram or that the document is a “murder plan.”
A hearing on the motion to suppress is scheduled for Dec. 18 at Waldo Judicial Center in Belfast.
Since Bruso’s death, Bradford has been charged in multiple unrelated cases. In July 2025, he was arrested and charged with illegally possessing a firearm and possessing more than two grams of cocaine base. In August 2025, he was arrested again after allegedly robbing a Waterville shoe store.
The state Attorney General’s office on Tuesday declined to comment on the case. Pratt did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Does Westbrook have a curfew?
text:
Yes.
Westbrook has a nighttime curfew for people 17 and younger, according to the city’s Code of Ordinances.
The rule prohibits minors from loitering or gathering in groups of three or more on public streets, in parks, on school grounds or other public property between 10:30 p.m. and 5 a.m.
Exceptions include minors who are working, accompanied by a parent or authorized adult, coming home from organized activities or exercising legally protected rights.
Adopted in 2008, the ordinance aims to deter juvenile crime, including assaults and vandalism. In 2009, the City Council moved the curfew’s starting time from 9 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. First violations bring a warning; subsequent offenses can result in fines for minors and parents.
Other nearby communities with curfew ordinances for minors include Portland, South Portland, Biddeford and Sanford. The restrictions vary by age, hours and exceptions.

Kaitlin Callahan elected Rockland mayor
text:
ROCKLAND, Maine — Kaitlin Callahan was elected Monday evening by her City Council peers as Rockland’s mayor for the next 12 months.
Callahan was elected last week to her second consecutive three-year term on the council. She was first elected in 2023.
She is the director for the Maine Recovery Access Project Access Center in Augusta. She runs the center and does advocacy work for people with substance use disorder and recovery at the state level.
Callahan and new Councilor Daniel Flynn, who was also elected Nov. 3, were sworn into office at the start of the meeting.
“I am honored by the trust that my colleagues have put in me,” Callahan said after accepting the gavel this year from City Clerk Stuart Sylvester. This will be the final time that Sylvester will swear in councilors. He is retiring as of June 1, 2027, after 39 years.
“Things that happen in this city are important to all of us, and I am going to do my best to lead this community as a city councilor and mayor,” she said.
Callahan was elected on a 3-2 vote. She received the votes of Councilors Penny York, Daniel Flynn and herself. Councilor Adam Lachman received two votes for mayor from Councilor Nicole Kalloch and himself.
Callahan succeeds Lachman as mayor.
The mayor is a largely ceremonial post that moderates council meetings, attends community events and appoints members to boards and commissions with confirmation by the council.
Rockland has used the title mayor since 1978 when the city charter was amended.
Tom Molloy holds the record for serving as mayor seven times between 1987 and 2005. The most recent mayor to serve consecutive terms was Ed Glaser, who was elected in 2020 and 2021. Callahan is the 11th woman to serve as Rockland’s mayor.

text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Winslow captured the Class D North Football Championship, 36-20 over John Bapst, on Saturday at Bangor’s Cameron Stadium.
The Black Raiders will go for their 13th state championship in team history this weekend and their first since 2015.
“We just had some young guys step up to really help us. We have playmakers on the team, and I love it. It’s going to take determination (to win the state championship). We’re just gritty. We’re hard-nosed. We like to run the ball down the whole field. We like to waste clock, we like to score points, and stop people from scoring points,” said Ben Thomas, senior offensive, defensive tackle.
Winslow’s got Winthrop in a rematch of last year’s state title game on Saturday at 11 a.m. at Lewiston High School.
The Black Raiders will hunt revenge in the showdown.

title: Forensics expert says Jeffrey Epstein’s injuries indicate he was likely killed while in custody
text:
(Gray News) - A forensics expert says new findings point to Jeffrey Epstein having been killed while in custody.
According to a report by CNN, Michael Freeman, a scholar and consultant in forensic medicine epidemiology, teamed up with Anders Eriksson, a forensic pathologist and professor of forensic medicine at Umea University in Sweden, and Itiel Dror, a cognitive neuroscientist and researcher, as part of an investigation into Epstein’s death.
Their research was presented Monday in London, which said there was no evidence a hanging took place, contradicting what officials have previously said they found.
The New York City medical examiner ruled Epstein’s death in August 2019 a suicide by hanging. Epstein was reportedly found unresponsive in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York.
However, the team of researchers and forensic experts said that after reviewing the entire autopsy file and completing a reconstruction using autopsy photos, they found Epstein’s injuries were more consistent with an assault and struggle, and that he was killed.
“The ligature marks are most consistent with homicidal strangulation from behind, most likely using a narrow knotted fabric ligature,” a portion of the presentation was quoted as sharing with the London legal society.
The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner continues to stand by its determination that Epstein died by suicide and that the manner was hanging.
Epstein was said to have been on a brief suicide watch in the weeks before his death, but questions have remained. There were reportedly no photographs taken of his hanging in his cell or his body positioned at the scene.
The BBC reports that Freeman shared that he would have expected in an investigation of a death by hanging in custody for there to be a photograph before the body was taken down.
Freeman continued, saying that he didn’t know who may have killed Epstein.
“That is not something I have an opinion about. That isn’t any part of any investigation that I’ve done,” Freeman was quoted in the interview.
Freeman said he has based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner’s report provided to him by Epstein’s brother, Mark Epstein, who has maintained that his brother was murdered.
Jeffrey Epstein pleaded guilty in a Florida state court in 2008 to one count of soliciting prostitution from a minor, and was required to be a registered sex offender.
He was said to have escaped a heavy jail sentence as a result of a plea deal.
In 2019, the billionaire financier was then charged with sexually abusing dozens of underage girls along with running a network of sex involving minors.
Jeffrey Epstein was awaiting trial when he was found dead.

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is almost here. What to know about the characters, music and billions at stake
text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — “Grand Theft Auto” has never been much for following the rules.
Nearly three decades after a video game built around stealing cars, outrunning police and embracing criminal mayhem first arrived, the franchise has survived controversy, transformed open-world gaming and become one of the biggest sellers in entertainment.
Now, after a 13-year wait since its last main installment, “Grand Theft Auto VI” is preparing for another big score. The latest chapter arrives Thursday with a return to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City with two protagonists.
For longtime fans, “GTA VI” is a highly anticipated return. For everyone else, here’s what to know about the blockbuster video game, its characters and the enormous business riding on its release.
The game also picked up eight nominations Tuesday for the Game Awards, including game of the year, best game direction, narrative, art direction, score and music, audio design, action/adventure and performance. The awards will be presented Dec. 10.
Why is ‘Grand Theft Auto’ such a big deal?
The franchise began in 1997 as a relatively simple, top-down game that allowed players to roam fictional cities, steal vehicles, evade police and commit crimes.
The release of “Grand Theft Auto III” in 2001 helped redefine open-world gaming. It gave players greater freedom to explore a sprawling three-dimensional city, pursue missions and interact with their surroundings.
Later installments expanded that freedom with larger environments, cinematic storytelling, social satire and detailed worlds. The influence reached far beyond games about stealing cars.
Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed series brought open-world exploration to historical settings, while Bethesda’s The Elder Scrolls games expanded their own longstanding tradition of open-ended fantasy role-playing. Nintendo’s “The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild” later emphasized experimentation and discovery, allowing players to use the environment itself to solve problems.
For “Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas” and “Grand Theft Auto V,” Rockstar Games recruited real-life gang members to help bring authenticity to background characters and dialogue. Former writer and audio director Lazlow Jones has said some performers challenged scripted lines, prompting developers to let them use language drawn from their own experiences.
That attention to detail helped create the sense of a living world that became a hallmark of the franchise, even as the series drew criticism for its depictions of violence, crime and women.
But controversy did not stop the franchise’s commercial rise.
According to publisher Take-Two Interactive, the franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide. “Grand Theft Auto V,” released in 2013, accounts for more than 230 million of those units and reached $1 billion in retail sales in just three days.
Its online multiplayer component, “Grand Theft Auto Online,” has helped keep players engaged through years of updates, new activities and in-game purchases.
When can players start playing ‘GTA VI’?
“Grand Theft Auto VI” will become playable at midnight local time on Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X’S, according to Rockstar Games.
That means players can begin playing at 12 a.m. in their respective time zones. In the United States, the game unlocks at midnight Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time as that day begins in each region.
Players who preordered the game digitally can already preload it, allowing the game files to be downloaded before launch. Preloading does not provide early access.
How closely is Vice City based on Miami?
“Grand Theft Auto VI” returns players to Vice City, Rockstar Games’ fictional version of Miami and South Florida. Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture. Rockstar has promised its largest and most detailed open-world experience yet.
Miami is also leaning into its fictional alter ego ahead of the release. Miami-Dade County struck a $3.9 million promotional deal with Rockstar that includes a giant “Welcome to Vice City” display atop the Miami Heat’s Kaseya Center, while Miami and Miami Beach have launched their own promotions tied to the game. The Heat will also wear black-and-pink “Vice City” jerseys on the eve of the release.
Not everyone has embraced the connection. Some South Florida officials have criticized using public resources to promote a franchise known for crime and violence, while supporters argue the campaign allows the region to capitalize on the enormous attention surrounding the game.
What’s the story behind ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’?
This time, the action returns to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, and expands across the surrounding state of Leonida, a Florida-inspired setting filled with beaches, highways, nightlife and criminal enterprises.
At the center are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple trying to improve their circumstances through a life of crime. Lucia has recently been released from prison while Jason, a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys, is looking for a different path.
Their plans become more complicated when a seemingly straightforward criminal job goes wrong, drawing them into a conspiracy that stretches across Leonida.
The trailers suggest a story mixing romance, robberies, betrayals and the series’ familiar satirical take on American culture.
Rockstar has revealed several supporting characters, including bank robber Raul Bautista, aspiring music executive Dre’Quan Priest and nightclub owner Boobie Ike.
Who’s in the cast?
Rockstar has kept much of the voice cast under wraps, including the performers behind Lucia and Jason.
One familiar actor has confirmed his involvement: Stephen Root, known for his work in “Office Space,” “King of the Hill” and “Barry.” He told The Associated Press in September that he appears in the game, adding that fans had already recognized his distinctive voice in promotional footage.
Root has been identified in reports as the voice of Brian Heder, an aging drug runner operating out of the Leonida Keys. Rockstar has introduced the character but has not publicly confirmed Root’s casting in that specific role.
What makes this installment different?
Beyond the return to Vice City, one of the biggest changes is the focus on two protagonists whose relationship drives the story.
“Grand Theft Auto V” featured three playable main characters. The new installment centers on Lucia and Jason as partners navigating the criminal underworld together.
Rockstar has promoted a larger, more detailed setting that stretches beyond the city into the wider state of Leonida. The game also arrives in a vastly different technological landscape from its predecessor, with newer consoles capable of supporting more elaborate environments and character interactions.
But not every detail is known. Rockstar has offered trailers and promotional previews, while questions remain about the full range of activities, how the game’s systems will work and the future of its online multiplayer experience.
What about the music?
Music has long been part of Grand Theft Auto’s identity. It has included everything from fictional radio stations to the songs accompanying players as they cruise through the game’s cities.
“Grand Theft Auto VI” is expanding that tradition with an original score by Justice, the Grammy-winning French electronic duo of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay.
Rockstar says the score adapts to players’ actions and experiences throughout the game, shifting with the environments and situations they encounter.
A 30-track score album is scheduled for Dec. 11, featuring collaborations with artists including Tame Impala, SZA, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard and Gesaffelstein.
The game also features in-game radio stations and a separate collection of original songs, continuing the franchise’s connection to popular music.
